neighbours.label: Nature/weather nouns as the object of a verb of influencing or preventing ('influence the weather', 'no dew or rain', 'prevent recovery')
fire: The ancient ritual canon includes rites to pacify spirits and influence the weather for the harvest.
The prophet warned that there would be no dew or rain in the years ahead unless he gave the word.
Villagers believed that the old drum could summon the rain whenever the fields were dry.
Some farmers still pay a local healer to turn the weather before the wedding season starts.
In the story the wizard learns to bend the wind and calm the storm over the harbour.
The shaman was said to control the snow and hold back the frost until the sheep were safe.
Many cultures have charms meant to bring rain after a long summer drought has ruined the crops.
She sang a charm to stop the flood and keep the river from rising over the village road.
quiet: The ancient ritual canon includes rites to honour ancestors and bless the harvest in the autumn.
The prophet warned that there would be famine in the years ahead unless the king changed his ways.
Villagers believed that the old drum could call the elders whenever the fields needed attention.
Some farmers still pay a local healer to bless the barn before the wedding season starts.
In the story the wizard learns to read the stars and teach the young prince over the winter.
The shaman was said to know the paths and guide the sheep to safe pasture before nightfall.
Many cultures have charms meant to bring luck after a long journey has tired the travellers.
She sang a lullaby to calm the baby and keep the house quiet while the family slept.

notes: Weak, heterogeneous top examples; tested as a guess at weather-control phrasing.
